key_insight: Finite-element-guided stressor layer patterning can sculpt a silicon crystal into a near-sinusoidal crystalline undulator with sub-millimeter period and nanometer-scale amplitude.
engineering_relevance: This shows a practical path from simulation to fabrication for compact gamma-ray sources using standard silicon processing and controlled residual stress.
method: Simulated silicon substrate deformation with FEM to tune geometry and suppress higher harmonics.
Patterned a silicon nitride stressor layer to induce periodic bending on a silicon (110) substrate.
Fabricated a 160 µm-thick undulator with 10 periods and 334 µm period length based on the optimized design.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful fabrication and a uniform deformation extending up to 20 µm from the surface, with the device targeted to emit 5–15 MeV gamma photons under 5–30 GeV beams.
watch_item: Performance depends on maintaining highly uniform sinusoidal deformation; higher-order distortions or fabrication nonuniformity could reduce channeling quality and radiation output.
paper_title: From Simulation to Fabrication: Realizing Silicon Crystalline Undulators with Silicon Nitride Stressor Layer Patterning
